display.purpose: Section titles on the main page, capitals.

address.purpose: The contact email set as display type.

lead.purpose: About paragraph, project descriptions, the line under a title.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Every entrance and press: wordmark rise, reveals, button press, lighting-pass swap.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Feedback on every button and chip.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: rise 28px with opacity on a view() scroll timeline, entry 0–75%, fill forwards
motion.purpose: Entrance of section parts; visible by default where scroll timelines are unsupported.

motion.name: tile-video
motion.purpose: Hover loop fading in over the poster.

motion.name: tile-dim
motion.purpose: Other tiles' media while one plays.

motion.name: pass-swap
motion.value: blur(6px) and 0.7 opacity to sharp over 240ms
motion.purpose: Bridges two lighting passes so they read as one light changing.

motion.name: intro
motion.value: letters-cut layer: hold 1500ms, scale(90) over 1100ms cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1), fade in last 250ms
motion.purpose: First load per session: the reel through the ULTEMA letters, which open to the full screen.

motion.name: film-name
motion.purpose: The reel's film name changing with the cut.

narrative.overview: ULTEMA is the automotive-CGI studio standard played straight, at the craft level of Fuze, Unit Image, The Mill and Platige. The film is always the largest thing on screen; the interface is a slim bar, a white wordmark and a few words. The page is warm black from top to bottom, and the only colour that is not the footage's own is a brass hover. It is a portfolio, not a sales page: no call-to-action buttons. What makes it ULTEMA and not a template: the site opens on black with the reel seen through the ULTEMA letters, which then open to the full screen (after The Mill, at the owner's request); the reel names the film on screen; the work is a wall where every film keeps the frame it was made in, 2.39:1 cinema beside 9:16 social and 1:1 product films.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed muted film in every first screen, with type on its lower edge over a neutral scrim and a second scrim under the bar.
Warm black ground with one tone step for second grounds; white ink; brass only as a hover.
Two faces: Unbounded 800 in capitals for titles, Onest for everything read.
Square corners, no lines, no shadows, no ornament.
Motion that comes from the films and the scroll, never decoration.

rules.name: The One Brass Rule
rules.body: Brass appears only where a pointer is: the hover of a link. Nothing rests in brass.

rules.name: The Tone-Step Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by stepping from Warm Black to Ember Black, never by a line or a shadow.

rules.name: The Footage Owns Colour Rule
rules.body: The interface keeps to black, white and brass; every other colour on the page comes from the films.

rules.name: The Five Steps Rule
rules.body: A page uses at most five sizes: label, body, lead, headline, display. The wordmark is drawn, not set, and sits outside the count.

rules.name: The Two Lines Rule
rules.body: Every heading holds two lines or fewer at every width; cut words before shrinking type.

rules.name: The True Frame Rule
rules.body: A film is shown in its own aspect. Never crop the wall to a uniform 16:9 grid.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. Neutral scrims on a film (under the hero type, under the bar) are the only gradients the system allows.

dos: Do open every page with a full-bleed film or a film at full height, muted, with a pause control; on the reel, always name the film on screen.
Do keep brass (#c9a45a) to hovers; nothing rests in brass.
Do show each film in its own aspect: 2.39:1, 9:16 or 1:1.
Do set titles in Unbounded 800 capitals and everything read in Onest.
Do keep content visible by default; entrances play only where the browser supports scroll timelines, and reduced motion keeps opacity changes only.
Do carry both languages in the markup and switch with the EN/RU pair, remembered per visitor.
donts: Don't use gradients, glows or shadows; the neutral scrims on the reel (under the hero type and under the bar) are the only exception.
Don't draw lines: no hairlines, outlined boxes or dividers. Step the tone instead.
Don't put small labels above headings, number sections 01/02/03, or set monospace.
Don't round corners; the About portrait's circle is the single exception.
Don't add a third typeface or a second accent colour.
Don't add sales calls to action ("Start a project" and the like); contact lives in the Contact section.
